default.headline: Competitive move ripples through {segment}; rivals re-price within 9 months
default.summary: {actor}'s {move} forces a measurable share shift in {segment}, but the magnitude depends on incumbent depth and switching cost.

year_1.title: Y1 — Announcement shock & first orders
events: {actor} announces {move}; trade press and analysts (Wohlers, SmarTech) publish takes within 30 days.
Top-3 incumbents in {segment} convene pricing reviews; 1 of 3 cuts list price within Q3.
Early-adopter customers (new-space, motorsport) place trial orders worth ~$8-15M cumulatively.
Materials suppliers wait — none reprice in Y1.

year_2.title: Y2 — Qualification cycle & defensive bundles
events: Aerospace/medical qualification cycles complete for early movers; production POs land.
At least one incumbent launches a defensive bundle (printer + materials + service credit).
A second-tier OEM signals openness to acquisition; bankers circulate teasers.
{actor}'s share gains accelerate but plateau as cert backlog forms.

year_3.title: Y3 — Consolidation or stabilization
events: Either a tier-2 OEM is acquired, or the industry settles into a new equilibrium with {actor} structurally larger.
Materials suppliers renegotiate volume tiers with the new leader.
End-customer base reports lower average price-per-part by 8-12% in {segment}.

agent_reactions.stance: Defensive — bundle pricing, hold list price
Counter-attack — emphasize throughput per dollar
Hold — lean on aerospace cert moat
Watch & wait until Y2 qualification data
Fast-switch if cost-per-part drops >15%
Neutral — open to supply whoever wins

risks: If {actor} posture is 'turnaround', credit risk may scare aerospace buyers away.
Tariff shock could blunt the price advantage in international segments.
Defensive M&A by an incumbent could lock up a key materials supplier.

default.headline: Value prop tested against {n_verticals} verticals — {hot} bites first, {cold} resists
default.summary: Simulated buyer agents score the value proposition. Verticals with throughput-per-dollar buy rules respond fastest; qualification-first verticals delay 12-18 months regardless of headline savings.

year_1.title: Y1 — Pilot & objection harvest
events: Pilot conversations open with 4-6 named accounts across selected verticals.
Top objections surface: 'show us the qualified material allowables', 'cost-per-part audit', 'service uptime SLAs'.
Throughput-driven verticals (dental, motorsport, new-space) sign 1-2 LOIs.
Qualification-first verticals (aerospace primes, medical implants) request 18-month data package.

year_2.title: Y2 — Reference customers & price discovery
events: First 2 reference customers go public at industry shows (Formnext, RAPID).
Competitive responses: at least one incumbent re-prices to within 8% of your offer.
Materials suppliers start quoting volume discounts contingent on co-marketing.
If price premium > +20%, dental and motorsport renegotiate; aerospace is unmoved either way.

year_3.title: Y3 — Production scale or repositioning
events: Throughput-driven verticals are at production scale, contributing 60-70% of bookings.
Aerospace primes complete first qualifications; revenue lags but margin is high.
Decision: double down on throughput verticals or invest 18-24 months building an aerospace specialist team.

agent_reactions.stance: Cautious — 'We need allowables and 24 months of process control data'
Bullish — 'If you can deliver in 8 weeks, we'll buy now'
Buy if cost-per-part beats current SLS workflow by >15%
Conditional — 'Show us cost parity with HPDC at 50k units/year'
Engage but lock in supplier diversity clause

risks: Premium pricing erodes if a low-cost Chinese OEM matches the throughput claim.
Aerospace qualification slip pushes ROI past 36 months.
Materials volatility breaks the cost-per-part case.

default.headline: Industrial AM grows to ~$32-38B by 2028 under '{capex_cycle}' capex; {tariff_regime} reshapes flows
default.summary: Top-down view of metal, polymer, and service-bureau segments under selected macro conditions.

year_1.title: Y1 — Macro setup
events: Capex regime '{capex_cycle}' sets baseline order book: industrial AM bookings move {capex_directional}.
Tariff regime '{tariff_regime}' shifts ~6-12% of metal-powder flows.
AI generative design at {ai_design_adoption}% adoption begins to expand the addressable parts catalog.

year_2.title: Y2 — Mid-cycle inflection
events: Multi-laser metal LPBF crosses cost-parity for selected aerospace brackets.
Service bureaus capture share from in-house print fleets; Xometry-style platforms grow ~22%.
M&A intensity at {consolidation}% drives at least 1 tier-2 OEM exit or merger.

year_3.title: Y3 — New equilibrium
events: Top-5 OEMs hold ~58% combined share (vs ~52% today) on consolidation.
Polymer commoditizes faster than metal; ASPs in polymer drop 9-14%.
Materials suppliers with vertically integrated certs (Sandvik, Carpenter) gain pricing power.

agent_reactions.stance: Defends metal aero cert moat; cedes mid-tier polymer
Pushes polymer cost curve; experiments with Metal Jet at scale
Aggressive throughput leader marketing
Increase AM share of new-program parts to 12-18%
Commoditize polymer powders; protect engineered grades
Hold pricing on Ni/Ti certs

risks: Recession scenario inverts metal growth to flat by Y3.
Tariff escalation fragments the global powder market.
Generative AI overshoots — bottleneck moves from design to qualification.

default.headline: {shock} hits {vertical} — magnitude {magnitude}/5, persistence {duration_quarters} quarters
default.summary: End-customer agents in {vertical} reprice their AM spend; OEMs and materials suppliers respond with a lag.

year_1.title: Y1 — Initial reaction
events: {vertical} reallocates ~{realloc_pct}% of category spend within 2 quarters.
OEMs serving the vertical see order-book volatility; the top 3 hold pricing, smaller OEMs cut.
Materials suppliers exposed to the shock signal hedging behavior in earnings calls.

year_2.title: Y2 — Structural rebalance
events: If shock is 'reshoring mandate' or 'feedstock spike': domestic powder capacity adds gain pricing power.
If shock is 'regulatory acceleration' or 'AI-driven geometry': adoption rate steps up by 2-4 percentage points.
At least one mid-tier OEM repositions explicitly toward the affected vertical.

year_3.title: Y3 — New baseline
events: Demand baseline in {vertical} settles at a level distinct from pre-shock — direction depends on shock type.
Cross-vertical spillover begins: adjacent verticals (e.g. defense → industrial machinery) inherit standards/tooling.
Reporting analysts revise 5-year industrial AM TAM by ±$2-4B.

agent_reactions.stance: Re-bid frame agreements within 2 quarters
Hold price; lean on cert moat
Aggressively undercut while incumbents are distracted
Pricing power if shock = feedstock
Opportunistic share gain if tariffs not blocking

risks: If duration <4 quarters, market snaps back and committed capex strands.
If magnitude 5/5, secondary effects in adjacent verticals dominate primary scenario.
Geopolitical overlay can invert tariff assumptions mid-simulation.
